english.title: Provide false / misleading material to licensing authority / ethics committee when conducting clinical trial

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a person who was conducting a clinical trial authorised in accordance with the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004, provided to

(A)_[the licensing authority,]_
(B)_[an ethics committee,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE LICENSING AUTHORITY / ETHICS COMMITTEE..), for the purposes of those Regulations, relevant information which was false or misleading in a material particular, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FALSE OR MISLEADING PARTICULAR..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 50(2)(a) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides that a person does not commit an offence under these Regulations if he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid the commission of that offence. Where evidence is adduced which is sufficient to raise an issue with respect to that defence, the court or jury shall assume that the defence is satisfied unless the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that it is not.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine

None
